references.text: The woman responds to Jesus' offer of "living water" in John 4:10. Here she now asks for this water, but still understands it in a literal, physical sense.

Jesus has just explained that whoever drinks the water he gives will never thirst again (John 4:13-14). The woman's request to "never thirst again" shows that she grasps the promise, yet does not yet understand its spiritual meaning.

A similar misunderstanding occurs in John 6:34-35, where the crowd asks Jesus for "the bread of life" without realizing that he himself is the bread. Jesus answers that whoever comes to him will never hunger, and whoever believes in him will never thirst.

In John 7:37-38, Jesus cries out that whoever is thirsty should come to him and drink, and that streams of living water will flow from within the believer. The theme of living water satisfying spiritual thirst remains the same.
The prophet Isaiah invites all who are thirsty to come to the waters (Isaiah 55:1). This Old Testament promise of spiritual satisfaction forms the background for Jesus' offer of living water.
In Revelation 21:6, God promises to give the thirsty free drink from the spring of the water of life, an eschatological fulfillment of the promise Jesus gives to the Samaritan woman.
Revelation 22:17 repeats the invitation: "Let the one who is thirsty come; let the one who wishes take the water of life without cost." This points back to Jesus' offer of living water.

In John 6:26-27, Jesus rebukes the crowd because they seek him for physical food rather than for the spiritual food that endures to eternal life. The woman's desire to avoid fetching water daily reflects a similar material motivation.
Isaiah 12:3 speaks of drawing water with joy from the springs of salvation. This prophetic image is part of the Old Testament background for the promise of living water that Jesus gives.

In John 3:4, Nicodemus misunderstands Jesus' words about being born again in a physical sense, just as the woman here misunderstands the living water. The Gospel of John repeatedly uses this technique of literal misunderstandings of spiritual truths.
